analysis:
The only changed line in this PR is head line 417 of docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds a documentation row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, which describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots, gated by a 128-token shader-cache probe and bounded to 20 seconds per engine. The row says the warmup trains no rate or counter and is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. Head line 417 is outside the excerpted head unit (lines 1-353), so I could not verify the row directly. I relied on the patch excerpt for it. The three supplied units are base lines 509-703 and head lines 1-353, which are surrounding context.

No source code, auth, attestation, encryption or coordinator wire behavior changes in this PR. The new env var affects local performance and warmup scheduling only. It does not touch the A-001 prompts, the A-003 key, the prefix-cache T-041 surfaces, or attestation/App Attest TB-011. Warmup runs synthetic inputs (a 128-token probe) and does not appear to use consumer data. I found no evidence in the supplied text that it persists artifacts or touches the SSD prefix cache. Whether the warmup path writes shader caches or interacts with the encrypted prefix cache or the TTFT timing oracle (SEC-035) is not verifiable from this documentation, and the implementing file (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) was not supplied.

Security-relevant doc note: the row says the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent, which is consistent with the documented passthrough allow-list pattern. The implementing allow-list change is unverified in the supplied evidence. Nothing here weakens the documented TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 boundaries. No finding qualifies. A reviewer of the code change, if any exists in other batches, should confirm that the warmup uses only synthetic prompts, that the shader-cache location is operator-private, and that the passthrough key list matches the documentation.
